y1: John the Baptist wore clothes made of camel's hair and had a leather belt around his waist. This was the appearance of the prophet Elijah in the Old Testament. After four hundred years without a prophet, a prophet appeared again in Israel.
y2: He was the "voice of one crying in the wilderness" spoken of by Isaiah. His message was short: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
y3: The wilderness is the place where Israel stayed for 40 years after leaving Egypt and came to know God. John called the people back to the wilderness so they could make a fresh start as they crossed the Jordan River. God started His new work not in a magnificent temple, but in the empty desert.
y5: John called the Pharisees and Sadducees who came to be baptized a "brood of vipers!" and told them to "produce fruit worthy of repentance."
y6: "Don't think to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.'" This means that a good family or religious background does not guarantee salvation.
y7: John's warning was not directed at those outside the faith, but at the most religious people. Going to church for a long time and growing up in a believing family are good things, but they cannot replace repentance.
y8: The Baptism of the Sinless One
y9: When Jesus came to be baptized, John tried to stop Him: "I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?"
y10: Jesus said, "Let it be so now, for it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way." Jesus stood in the same line as sinners.
y11: Jesus had no sin to confess, but He identified Himself with sinners. This scene foreshadows the cross: a sinless One standing in the place of sinners. This is exactly what the Gospel is.
y12: The Opened Heavens, the Heard Voice
y13: When Jesus came up out of the water, the heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice was heard: "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."
y14: These words combine Psalm 2:7 (the Kingly Son) and Isaiah 42:1 (the suffering servant). Jesus is both the King and the suffering Servant.
y15: These words were spoken before Jesus had performed even a single miracle. God's love is not a reward given for success. Identity comes first, and then comes the mission.
verse: “And a voice came out of the heavens, saying, ‘This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.’”
prayer: Lord God, thank You that the sinless Jesus stood in the place of sinners. Help me to repent in a way that changes the direction of my life, not just with words. Help me to stand on the truth that I am Your beloved child, not on my successes. I pray in the name of Your beloved Son, Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: John the Baptist. He was the son of the priest Zechariah and was born six months before Jesus. He received the mission to prepare the way for the Messiah. Jesus called him "the greatest among those born of women" (11:11).
d1: Isaiah. A prophet who lived in the 8th century BC. He spoke many prophecies about Immanuel and the suffering servant. The prophecy of Immanuel in the first lesson is also in the book of Isaiah (7:14).
d2: Repent. It means "to change (meta) the mind (noia)." It is not just staying in a feeling of regret, but changing the direction of one's life. Jesus' first sermon also begins with the word "Repent" (4:17).
d3: the kingdom of heaven. This is not just a place to go after death, but the reality of God ruling as King. Matthew says "of heaven" for Jewish readers who were careful about using God's name. In the Gospel of Matthew, "the kingdom of heaven" appears more than thirty times.
d4: Pharisees. It was a devout movement that strictly followed the law and was respected by the people. But there was a danger of focusing only on outward appearances. They were the ones who argued with Jesus the most (chapter 23).
d5: Holy Spirit. He is the Spirit of God. He gives Jesus power for ministry and lives inside believers. John said that Jesus would baptize "with the Holy Spirit and fire" (3:11).
